notes: An NSQF-aligned short-term qualification approved by NSQC and listed on India's National Qualification Register; HARTRON is the awarding body. No delivering centre has been verified.
Stores the 5 modules and the 18 performance criteria of 'Introduction to Accounting with Tally' (the computerised-accounting module); performance criteria of the other modules are not stored.
Tally is the accounting package named; the NYSC course names Peachtree, Sage, MYOB and QuickBooks. Comparison is at the level of computerised-accounting competencies, not specific products.
scope_verbatim: The course helps to develop skills in basics of computers and accounting to automate and integrate all business operations.
Candidate is expected to maintain financial records both manually and using Tally and is also expected to perform other office task using office automation tools.

The Certificate IV in Accounting and Bookkeeping (FNS40222) was inspected but not used: it is a higher-level bookkeeping qualification, whereas the NYSC course is a 6-month part-time software course.
scope_verbatim: This qualification reflects the role of individuals with functions that could include financial data entry, processing accounts and payrolls, providing customer service in financial transactions, and producing financial reports.

modules.outcome_verbatim: On completion of this module, students should be able to support essential business operations by differentiating the various functions in an enterprise, compute employee payroll, prepare documents to support international trade, handle monetary transactions, compute accounting equation and record business transactions in source documents.
On completion of module, students should be able to apply sales techniques to sell to client needs and develop strong sales relationships.
On completion of the module, students should be able to apply the knowledge of accounting theories and relate to business scenarios, and record business transactions.

On completion of the module, students should be able to determine the value of stock, prepare Trial Balance, Bank Reconciliation, Statement of Comprehensive Income and Statement of Financial Position.
On completion of the module, students should be able to adopt the fundamental ethics and standards of behaviour expected of an accounting professional.
On completion of the module, students should be able to prepare cash budget, cash flow statements, analyse financial statements and propose business finance options in a business.

On completion of the module, students should be able to gain an overview of the Singapore income tax system and its tax administration and be able to prepare computations of tax liability for resident individuals. This module covers employment income and other sources of income, types of deductions and personal reliefs.
On completion of the module, students should be able to apply basic costing concepts to ascertain costs associated with the production of goods.
On completion of the module, students should be able to maintain the fixed asset register, adjust entries to account receivables and prepare control accounts.
On completion of the module, students should be able to correct errors, prepare balance day adjustments and adjusted final accounts.

On completion of the module, students should be able to prepare tax computations of tax liability for resident companies in Singapore and Goods and Services Tax (GST) returns for businesses. This module covers taxability of income, types of deductions and tax allowances available to reduce the chargeable income of a company.
On completion of the module, students should be able to prepare financial statements for partnership, cash budget and financial statements for limited companies.

On completion of the module, students should be able to gain an overview of traditional and cloud accounting software. Students should be able to navigate accounting functions within the software by integrating their accounting knowledge with the use of the accounting software.
